items.title: Admissible constraint classes and restricted identifiability

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.2
Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Lecture 1 §1.2

items.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real vector spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, and let $A:X\to Y$ be linear. The corresponding inverse-problem model has admissible truths $U$ and forward map $A|_U$. An **admissible constraint class** is a nonempty subset $C\subseteq U$; its constrained forward map is the restriction $A|_C:C\to Y$. The class $C$ is **identifiable for $A$** if $A|_C$ is injective, meaning $Ax=Ax'$ for $x,x'\in C$ implies $x=x'$. Define the difference set and kernel by

$$C-C:=\{x-x':x,x'\in C\},\qquad \ker A:=\{x\in X:Ax=0_Y\}.$$

items.title: A constraint removes kernel ambiguity exactly when its differences avoid the kernel

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.2
Tristan van Leeuwen and Christoph Brune, 10 Lectures on Inverse Problems and Imaging, Lecture 1 §1.2

items.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be real vector spaces, let $A:X\to Y$ be linear, and let $C\subseteq X$ be nonempty. The restriction $A|_C:C\to Y$ is injective if and only if

$$ (C-C)\cap\ker A=\{0\}. $$

This condition characterizes exact uniqueness on $C$; it gives no stability bound for perturbed data.

items.title: Finite-budget regularized gradient on a Stiefel constraint

references.title: P.-A. Absil, R. Mahony, and R. Sepulchre, Optimization Algorithms on Matrix Manifolds, Chapter 3 (2008)
references.locator: Example 3.6.2: real Stiefel tangent space, induced Frobenius metric, and orthogonal projection.

references.title: P.-A. Absil, R. Mahony, and R. Sepulchre, Optimization Algorithms on Matrix Manifolds, Chapter 4 (2008)
references.locator: Example 4.1.3: polar and QR retractions on the real Stiefel manifold.

references.title: Nicolas Boumal, An Introduction to Optimization on Smooth Manifolds (2023 prepublication)
references.locator: §§3.8 and 7.3: embedded-manifold gradients, Stiefel tangent/projection formulas, and the polar retraction.

items.statement:
For integers $1\le p\le n$, define the real Stiefel constraint set

$$\operatorname{St}(n,p):=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}:X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p\}.$$

Equip $\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with the Frobenius inner product $\langle U,V\rangle_F=\operatorname{tr}(U^{\mathsf T}V)$ and norm $\|U\|_F=\sqrt{\langle U,U\rangle_F}$. Let $H=\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, let $Y$ be a real Hilbert space, let $U\subseteq H$ be open and contain $\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be continuously Fréchet differentiable. Given data $y\in Y$, a reference matrix $X_{\rm ref}\in H$, and $\lambda\ge0$, define the residual and regularized objective by

$$r(X):=\|F(X)-y\|_Y,\qquad \Phi(X):=\tfrac12\|F(X)-y\|_Y^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|X-X_{\rm ref}\|_F^2.$$

Supply an ambient gradient oracle $G:U\to H$ satisfying $D\Phi(X)[Z]=\langle G(X),Z\rangle_F$ for every $X\in U$ and $Z\in H$, an initial frame $X_0\in\operatorname{St}(n,p)$, a residual tolerance $\tau\ge0$, a finite integer budget $K\ge0$, and a step schedule $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{K-1}$ with every $\alpha_k>0$. For a square matrix $M$, put $\operatorname{sym}(M):=(M+M^{\mathsf T})/2$. The procedure is:

1. Set the current frame to $X_0$ and the schedule index to $k=0$. If $r(X)\le\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$.
2. While $k<K$, compute $G(X)$ and the Stiefel gradient $g:=G(X)-X\operatorname{sym}(X^{\mathsf T}G(X))$. If $g=0$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{stationary})$.
3. Set $\eta:=-\alpha_k g$ and form the polar-retracted candidate

   $$X_{\rm trial}:=(X+\eta)\bigl((X+\eta)^{\mathsf T}(X+\eta)\bigr)^{-1/2}.$$

4. Evaluate $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})$ and $r(X_{\rm trial})$. If $\Phi(X_{\rm trial})>\Phi(X)$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{objective-rejected})$. Otherwise accept $X_{\rm trial}$ as the current frame. If its residual is at most $\tau$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{target-met})$; otherwise increment $k$ by one and repeat the loop.
5. When $k=K$, return $(X,r(X),\texttt{budget-exhausted})$.

This procedure is restricted to the stated finite-dimensional real Stiefel constraint and the displayed polar retraction. It gives no convergence, global-optimality, or noisy-data stability guarantee, and it makes no finite-precision claim. It does not apply to positivity constraints or other nonlinear manifolds without a separately specified compatible retraction and proof.

items.title: The Stiefel gradient procedure returns a feasible iterate within its finite budget

references.title: P.-A. Absil, R. Mahony, and R. Sepulchre, Optimization Algorithms on Matrix Manifolds, Chapter 4 (2008)
Nicolas Boumal, An Introduction to Optimization on Smooth Manifolds (2023 prepublication)

items.statement: For every input satisfying the finite-budget Stiefel gradient procedure, it returns after at most $K$ trial evaluations with an output frame $X_{\rm out}\in\operatorname{St}(n,p)$. Every accepted update has nonincreasing objective value, and the returned status is `target-met` exactly when $r(X_{\rm out})\le\tau$; every other returned status has $r(X_{\rm out})>\tau$.

title: Physical constraints and manifold-valued inversion — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A negative finite-difference PDE state is rejected before solving
items.statement: Discretize $-u''=f$ on $(0,1)$ with $u(0)=u(1)=0$ using grid points $x_i=i/3$ for $i=0,1,2,3$ and the two interior values $u_i=u(x_i)$, $z=(u_1,u_2)$. Put $h=1/3$ and define the centered stencil at $i=1,2$ by $D_hu_i=(2u_i-u_{i-1}-u_{i+1})/h^2$, with boundary values $u_0=u_3=0$. The resulting finite-difference system is $A_hz=f_h$, where $A_h=h^{-2}\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ and $f_h=(f(x_1),f(x_2))$. Impose the physical constraint $C=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb R^2:z_1\ge0,\ z_2\ge0\}$ for nonnegative nodal concentration. An input validator that checks both coordinates before invoking the linear solver rejects the candidate $z=(-1,1)$ before solving because its first coordinate is negative.

items.title: A line constraint removes one kernel direction
items.statement: Let $A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $A(s,t)=s$, and restrict the truth class to $C_0=\{(t,0):t\in\mathbb R\}$. Every scalar datum $y\in\mathbb R$ has exactly one admissible preimage, and $(C_0-C_0)\cap\ker A=\{0\}$; this constraint removes the vertical null direction.

items.title: A half-space constraint leaves a continuous kernel ambiguity
items.statement: Let $A:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ be $A(s,t)=s$, and restrict the truth class to the half-space $C_+=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb R^2:t\ge0\}$. For every datum $y\in\mathbb R$, the constrained fiber is $\{(y,t):t\ge0\}$, a continuous half-line of admissible truths; moreover $(C_+-C_+)\cap\ker A=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}\ne\{0\}$.
